title: Cargo workspace and crate skeletons
description: Create the Cargo workspace (resolver 2, edition 2024, MSRV pinned) with exactly the 12 crates named in CONTRACT.md: at-model, at-fs, at-adapters, at-store, at-engine, at-db, at-mcp, at-secrets, at-git, at-migrate, at-cli, at-app. Pin shared dependencies in [workspace.dependencies]: tauri 2 (+ tauri-build), ts-rs, tokio 1, rusqlite bundled, toml_edit, jsonc-parser, notify 8 + notify-debouncer-full, similar, saphyr, keyring, tracing, directories. Create module skeletons matching the contract (at-fs::{diff,backup,atomic,concurrency,symlink,watch}; at-app::app::{commands,bridge,state,menu} and ui/src/{shell,theme,components,screens,overlays,state,bridge}). at-app builds a binary named agentuna-app with an empty Tauri window (1200x800, title AgenTuna) that loads the Vite + React + TypeScript frontend in ui/; at-cli builds agentuna with a stub --version. Add rust-toolchain.toml, rustfmt.toml, deny.toml, and a root README build section.
acceptance: `cargo metadata --no-deps` lists exactly the 12 contract crates with the expected package names and paths.
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on macOS arm64 with `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings` and emits no warnings.
Every module named in CONTRACT.md exists with a `//!` doc comment and compiles as an empty stub; `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` succeeds.

`pnpm --dir ui tauri dev` opens a 1200x800 window titled AgenTuna that renders data returned by a Rust command, and `pnpm --dir ui build` typechecks and bundles; `cargo run -p at-cli -- --version` prints the workspace version.
`cargo fmt --check` passes, and `rust-toolchain.toml` pins one stable channel plus rustfmt and clippy components.
notes: Every other story assumes this layout. Epic is nominal: pure foundation serves all epics. No new crates beyond the contract list.

title: at-model domain types
description: Implement the plain domain types in at-model with no IO and no async: Scope (Global, User, Project, Local; precedence 0..3 where Local is nearest and writable), ItemKind (Skill, McpServer, Rule), ItemId (opaque `itm_` + UUIDv7 allocated once, survives rename and scope move), AgentId (claude_code, codex, omp, cursor, custom:<name>), Agent, Deployment { state: ItemState, mode: LinkMode, target_path, store_hash, target_hash, baseline_hash, sync_label }, ItemState (Linked, Off, Native, Conflict, Drifted), SyncLabel (InSync, ProjectOnly, LibraryNewer, ProjectNewer), Lock { scope, item_id, reason, locked_by, locked_at }, Preset. All enums get serde rename_all snake_case, Display/FromStr, and an explicit wire-name table.
acceptance: Scope::precedence orders Global < User < Project < Local; Scope::from_str accepts global/user/project/local case-insensitively, serde accepts only the lowercase wire names, and invalid input lists all four values.
ItemId::new() returns a fresh `itm_<uuidv7>`; two calls differ, ids sort by creation time (UUIDv7), and Display/FromStr round-trip an opaque id without encoding kind, scope or slug.
ItemId parsing rejects ids without the `itm_` prefix, malformed UUIDs and the old `kind:scope:slug` shape with a typed ItemIdError; no code path derives an id from a name or path.
Snapshot tests lock JSON wire names for Scope, ItemState, SyncLabel, LinkMode and AgentId; Scope::Local serializes as local and is treated as writable by is_writable().
A test greps at-model/src for std::fs, std::net, rusqlite, tokio and anyhow usage and fails if found; the crate depends only on serde, thiserror, uuid with the v7 feature, and time.
notes: Decision 1: ItemId is owned here and is the DB primary key. Decision 4: Local is a real writable scope, not a UI label.

title: at-db SQLite connection, migrations runner, schema v1
description: Open the SQLite index with rusqlite bundled. File databases use WAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000 ms, synchronous=NORMAL; memory databases disable WAL. Implement a migrations runner (rusqlite_migration or refinery) that applies embedded SQL in one transaction per version and records (version, applied_at, sha256) in `schema_version`. Migration v1 creates only `schema_version` and installs the runner; it creates no domain tables. Per decision 15, TF-011..TF-018 own the numbered migrations v2..v9 that create projects, agents, agent_paths, items, item_versions, deployments, native_items, locks, health_checks, sources, operations, operation_files, backups, drift_events, presets, preset_members, preset_applications, preset_application_members, settings, secret_refs, secret_ref_uses and remote_backup_state. Expose Db::open(path), Db::open_memory(), Db::migrate(), Db::connection() and a read-only connection factory.
acceptance: Opening a fresh file with only v1 registered applies v1 and leaves exactly one schema_version row (version=1, sha256 of the migration SQL); no domain table exists after v1.
Running migrate twice is a no-op: applied_at and row count are unchanged and no error is returned.
Editing a shipped migration changes its checksum and the next open fails with MigrationChecksumMismatch naming version and both hashes, without modifying the database.
Opening a database with schema_version greater than the binary supports fails with SchemaTooNew { found, supported } and leaves the file byte-identical.

A migration registered after v1 is applied once, in order, and a failing statement rolls back that version without recording it; a foreign-key error surfaced by v2+ is returned as DbError::Constraint, not a panic.
notes: All later DB stories add tables through new migration files; v1 is the only baseline. Migration SQL is embedded with include_str!, not read at runtime.

title: at-fs safe write pipeline (diff, backup, atomic write, concurrency check)
description: Implement WriteRequest { path, new_bytes, expected: ExpectedState (Absent | Hash | HashAndMtime), backup: BackupPolicy (None | OperationFolder(PathBuf)), follow_symlink: bool (default false), mode: Create|Replace, allow_empty_dir } and apply() in at-fs. Order: read current state, compare against expected, render a unified diff with `similar` (3 context lines), copy the current bytes into the caller-supplied operation backup folder (TC-014 owns the layout), create a temp file in the same directory with O_EXCL and mode 0600/0644, write and fsync it, re-read and re-hash the destination immediately before rename, rename over it, fsync the directory, then emit WriteOutcome { diff, backup_path, before_hash, after_hash, bytes, wrote_through_symlink }. follow_symlink=false opens the destination with O_NOFOLLOW and returns SymlinkRefused for a symlink; follow_symlink=true resolves the link, writes the target, and reports both the link path and the resolved path; only agent config writers may set it true. Failures remove the temp file and leave the original untouched.
acceptance: With expected=Hash(H) and a file hashing to H, apply writes the new bytes, returns a 3-context unified diff, and creates the backup inside the caller-supplied operation folder with before_hash equal to H; after_hash equals sha256 of the new bytes.

If the file's hash differs from expected, apply returns ConcurrentModification { path, expected, actual } and writes nothing; an injected external write between read and rename is also caught by the pre-rename re-hash.
Permission denied on the parent directory (mode 0500) returns FsError::PermissionDenied { path } with no temp file and no backup orphan left behind.
A SIGKILL failpoint between backup creation and rename leaves the original bytes readable; on next start TF-027 finds the temp and backup entry and the original remains unchanged.

With follow_symlink=false a symlink destination returns SymlinkRefused and both link and target bytes are unchanged; with follow_symlink=true the resolved target contains the new bytes, the link is preserved, and wrote_through_symlink=true records both paths.
notes: Decision 5/6: follow_symlink is off by default and only agent config writers enable it. Backups go into the caller's operation folder; layout is TC-014's.

title: at-fs refuse-to-overwrite guard
description: Implement classify_target(path, item_id, agent_id, scope) -> Managed | Unmanaged { kind: File|Dir|Entry, existing_hash } | Absent. Managed means the path lives under an AgenTuna store root or a deployments row links that exact path for the same item, agent and scope. Deployment or copy over an existing unmanaged file or non-empty directory returns RefusedOverwrite { path, kind, existing_hash, remedies: [Adopt, MoveAside, Cancel] } and writes nothing. Empty directories are refused unless allow_empty_dir=true. Re-run the check immediately before rename so a file created between preview and apply is still refused. Parent directories are created only when the target itself is absent.
acceptance: Deploying to an existing unmanaged `~/.claude/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md` returns RefusedOverwrite with the absolute path and both remedies; sha256 before and after are equal.
A path already recorded in deployments for the same item/agent/scope is allowed to update and keeps one row.
An unmanaged directory containing any file is refused wholesale (no merge, no partial copy); an empty directory is refused unless allow_empty_dir=true.
If an unmanaged file appears after preview but before rename, apply returns RefusedOverwrite and the new file's bytes are untouched.
Moving a refused target aside renames it to `<name>.agentuna-backup-<UTC timestamp>` inside the same parent, records the rename in operations, and never deletes bytes.
notes: Guard is unconditional and not gated by any setting or feature flag.

title: at-fs symlink/copy deployment primitive
description: Implement the deployment primitive in at-fs: link_dir(canonical_store, agent_path, LinkMode) creates a relative symlink when source and target share a volume and an absolute symlink otherwise; copy_dir writes a recursive copy plus `.agentuna-copy-manifest.json` (per-file sha256 + source version). Replacement is atomic: create `.<name>.agentuna-tmp-<pid>` next to the target, then rename over it. Detect EPERM/ENOTSUP on symlink and EXDEV on rename; return LinkUnsupported or fall back to copy only when the caller asked for LinkMode::Copy. Remove only paths that are recorded as owned deployments; never remove canonical store content. cfg(windows) uses junction for directories (TF-038).
acceptance: link_dir produces a symlink whose readlink resolves to the canonical store item directory; editing a file in the store is immediately visible through the agent path.
Replacing an existing link never exposes ENOENT to a concurrent reader; a 1000-iteration loop of readlink during replacement succeeds every time.
With an injected EPERM from symlink and LinkMode::Symlink, the call returns LinkUnsupported and leaves the target absent; with LinkMode::Copy it creates the copy plus manifest and reports mode=copy.
A copy deployment updates only files whose hash differs from the manifest on re-deploy; unchanged files keep mtime.
Deleting a deployment removes the link or copy and its manifest but the canonical item's file hashes are unchanged.
notes: Setting copy-vs-link is per agent (TF-023); WCAG/security review not needed. Windows junction behaviour is TF-038.

title: at-fs file watcher service with debounce
description: Implement WatchService over notify 8 + notify-debouncer-full. Watch the user store, the active project store, and every detected agent path from agent_paths (skills dir, mcp file, rules file). Debounce window 300 ms, event batching into WatchBatch { paths, kinds, observed_at }. Ignore `.git/`, `node_modules/`, `.agentuna/cache/`, `.agentuna/backups/`, `*.agentuna-tmp-*`, `*.swp`. Suppress self-writes for 2 s using a recent-write registry fed by TF-004 WriteOutcome (path + after_hash + time). Bounded channel capacity 1024; on overflow emit one RescanRequired. Deleting a watched path moves the watch to the nearest existing ancestor and re-adds children when the path returns.
acceptance: Fifty writes to `~/.claude.json` within 200 ms produce exactly one WatchBatch containing that path after at most 500 ms.
An AgenTuna write through TF-004 produces zero WatchBatch events (registry suppression verified by a counter).
Events under `.git/`, `node_modules/` and backup directories never appear in a batch; renames are reported once with old and new paths.
A 10k-file burst produces one RescanRequired and the service keeps running; queue memory stays bounded.
stop() joins within 1 s and releases FSEvents handles; calling start twice returns AlreadyRunning; deleting a watched project store yields PathGone and no crash.
notes: Watcher is a foundation for drift detection (TC-012) and agents screen rescan. Debounce and ignore rules live in one config struct so tests can shorten them.

title: app async bridge (tokio runtime, job handles, Tauri events)
description: Implement `at-app::app::bridge`: one tokio multi-thread runtime owned by the app (created on first use, shut down on exit); `spawn_job(JobSpec) -> JobHandle` with id, name, cancel token and progress sender; a job registry; and a bounded mpsc channel drained by one forwarder task that emits typed Tauri events (job progress, job finished) to the webview. Every state change emits exactly one event. Progress events are coalesced to at most 10 per second. Panics inside a job are caught with catch_unwind, converted to JobError::Panic { message } and logged with operation id. On app quit, cancel all jobs, wait up to 5 s, and mark still-running jobs Interrupted in the operations log.
acceptance: A 2-second simulated job started from a button keeps webview frame time under 16 ms and the UI renders the success state from the finished event without any mouse move or key press.
A job emits 10k progress ticks and the UI receives at most 10 updates per second while the final state arrives exactly once as Succeeded, Failed or Cancelled.
Cancel on a JobHandle stops the job within 100 ms and any late result is dropped by job id.
A job that panics becomes Failed { kind: Panic, message } and the process keeps running; the panic text appears in the log with the job id.
Quitting with three in-flight jobs exits within 5 s and each unfinished job has one operations row with status interrupted.
notes: All long-running UI work (health checks, scans, migration, git fetch) must go through this bridge; blocking the Tauri main thread or running a synchronous command that does long work is a review defect.

title: operations log (audit/history) write API
description: Implement `at-db::ops`: begin(kind, scope, actor, summary, correlation_id, undo_of) -> OperationId (ULID), attach_file(op, path, action, before_hash, after_hash, backup_id, bytes_before, bytes_after), and finish(op, status, error_kind). Kinds: Deploy, Undeploy, EditSkill, EditMcp, EditRule, Migrate, Adopt, Restore, Backup, Scan, Settings, Update, DriftAdopt, DriftRestore, SyncPush, SyncPull, RemoteBackup, RemoteRestore, Undo, Delete, Promote, Move, PresetApply, PresetUnapply, Lock, Unlock. Actor: ui, cli, migration, watcher, updater. Each operation and its files commit in one transaction. Queries: recent_changes(limit, scope, kind, since), operation_detail(id), undo_file_list(id). Operation rows are append-only; no update path may change kind, scope or started_at.
acceptance: A successful deploy writes one operations row with status=succeeded and one operation_files row per touched file with action created|modified|deleted and both hashes; the kind enum accepts all 26 names and rejects unknown strings.
A failed operation writes status=failed with error_kind and still records every file it touched; file rows are not rolled back when atomic=false.
recent_changes(limit=50) returns newest-first rows joined to item name and agent display name in under 20 ms on a 3k-item fixture.
Two processes (CLI and app) can begin and finish operations concurrently without lost rows or SQLITE_BUSY escaping after the 5 s timeout.
undo_file_list(id) returns the inverse actions and flags files whose current hash differs from after_hash as conflicted; operations never deleted by any API.
notes: Recent changes timeline (F03) and skill history (F06) read this API. The DB schema story is TF-016; this story is the write/query API.

title: test harness: temp HOME fixture with fake agent folders
description: Build the shared test fixture used by every crate. To avoid inventing a crate, place it in at-fs behind feature `testkit` as `at_fs::testkit` and re-export with dev-dependency features. TestHome creates a unique temp dir and builds an AppPaths rooted there for injection into code under test; an optional EnvScope sets HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA under a process-wide serialized guard for the few APIs that still read process env, and restores the previous values on Drop, including after panic. Fixture builders: install_claude_code(), install_codex(), install_omp(), install_cursor(), install_custom_agent(name, root); each writes realistic config files (JSON/JSONC/TOML/Markdown) with one skill and one MCP server. Helpers: empty_home(), project(name) with .mcp.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .agents/skills, and snapshot(dir) -> BTreeMap<relative path, sha256>. Never touches the real home directory.
acceptance: TestHome::new() creates a fresh dir per call and 8 parallel tests using AppPaths injection never observe each other's files; tests that need process env run under the serialized EnvScope and restore the previous values on drop.

install_claude_code() creates ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, ~/.claude.json with one mcpServers entry and CLAUDE.md; install_codex() creates ~/.codex/config.toml with one [mcp_servers.<name>] table, ~/.agents/skills and AGENTS.md.
snapshot(dir) returns sorted relative paths mapped to sha256 and detects a single-byte change without following symlinks outside dir.
empty_home() yields zero detected agents from detect_all() and zero items from a store scan.
TestHome::project("acme") creates the project fixture and registers its path; dropping the fixture removes the temp tree and restores env exactly.
notes: Dev-dependency only; production builds exclude the feature. No real config file from the developer machine is read or copied into fixtures.

title: DB schema: projects, agents, agent_paths
description: Migration v2. `projects(id TEXT PK, name TEXT, path TEXT UNIQUE, config_hash TEXT, last_opened_at, created_at, is_global INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)`. `agents(id TEXT PK, display_name TEXT, kind TEXT, version TEXT, installed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, managed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, detected_at, settings_json TEXT)`. `agent_paths(id INTEGER PK, agent_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, scope TEXT, kind TEXT CHECK(kind IN ('skills_dir','mcp_file','rules_file','settings_file','managed_dir','other')), path TEXT, format TEXT CHECK(format IN ('json','jsonc','toml','markdown','dir','yaml')), is_primary INTEGER, exists INTEGER, verified INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, is_override INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, UNIQUE(agent_id, scope, kind, path))`. Indexes: projects(path COLLATE NOCASE), agents(installed), agent_paths(agent_id), agent_paths(path), agent_paths(scope). Rebuildable from files: agents and agent_paths yes (detection); projects partially (paths rediscovered by scan, last_opened_at is user state).
acceptance: Upserting the same project path twice, including a path differing only in letter case on macOS, yields one row and updates last_opened_at.
Deleting an agent cascades to all agent_paths rows; deleting an item does not touch agents.

A detected Claude Code install writes one agents row with managed=1 and rows for skills_dir, mcp_file (~/.claude.json), rules_file (CLAUDE.md) and settings_file with verified=0 and is_override=0; exists flips to 0 after the path is removed and the row is kept.
Insert with an unknown agent_id fails with a foreign-key error; UNIQUE(agent_id,scope,kind,path) rejects duplicates; migration v1 to v2 applies in one transaction and leaves schema_version at 2.
Setting managed=0 keeps the agent and all agent_paths rows; verified=1 and is_override=1 round-trip, and defaults for new agents/paths are managed=1, verified=0, is_override=0.
notes: Projects are indexed for the project picker (TC slice owns detection). Rebuild semantics: see TF-019.

title: DB schema: items, item_versions
description: Migration v3. `items(id TEXT PK, kind TEXT CHECK(kind IN ('skill','mcp_server','rule')), scope TEXT CHECK(scope IN ('global','user','project','local')), project_id TEXT NULL, slug TEXT, name TEXT, source_path TEXT, content_hash TEXT, state TEXT, source_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES sources(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, enabled_default INTEGER, tags_json TEXT, created_at, updated_at, last_scanned_at)`. ItemId is the opaque `itm_` UUIDv7 from TF-002; uniqueness is a CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on (kind, scope, COALESCE(project_id,''), slug). `item_versions(id INTEGER PK, item_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, scope, content_hash, path, size, mtime, captured_at, version_label, UNIQUE(item_id, content_hash))`. Indexes: items(kind, scope), items(project_id), items(name COLLATE NOCASE), items(source_id), items(content_hash), item_versions(item_id, captured_at DESC). Rebuildable from files: yes; item_versions is populated by scanning store copies and can be fully rebuilt.
acceptance: The same kind+scope+project_id+slug cannot be inserted twice; the same slug under a different project_id or scope is allowed.
Inserting an item with scope local is accepted and returned by a scope filter; items.id values are opaque itm_ ids and never equal a slug or path.
Renaming an item or moving it between scopes keeps items.id unchanged and updates slug/scope; item_versions keeps history for the same id.
Deleting an item cascades its item_versions rows; deleting a source sets items.source_id NULL.
Seeding 3k items and 9k versions completes in under 100 ms on an in-memory database, and a scan with unchanged content adds no new item_versions row.
notes: Decision 1: id is the stable primary key; decision 4: scope includes 'local'.

title: DB schema: deployments
description: Migration v4. `deployments(id INTEGER PK, item_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, agent_id TEXT NOT NULL, scope TEXT, project_id TEXT NULL, state TEXT CHECK(state IN ('linked','off','native','conflict','drifted')), mode TEXT CHECK(mode IN ('symlink','copy','native','none')), target_path TEXT, link_target TEXT, store_hash TEXT, target_hash TEXT, baseline_hash TEXT, sync_label TEXT CHECK(sync_label IN ('in_sync','project_only','library_newer','project_newer')), updated_at, last_verified_at, operation_id TEXT NULL)`. Unique matrix index on (item_id, agent_id, scope, COALESCE(project_id,'')). Indexes: deployments(agent_id, scope), deployments(project_id), deployments(target_path), deployments(state), deployments(sync_label), deployments(item_id). Rebuildable from files: mostly yes by inspecting link targets, copy manifests and file hashes; `off` rows are rebuilt from the agent's disable lists; sync_label is recomputed by TA-005, never trusted from disk.
acceptance: The matrix cell (item, agent, scope, project_id) is unique; toggling off then on updates one row, never inserts a second.

store_hash is the AgenTuna copy hash, target_hash the deployed file or link-target hash, baseline_hash the last synced hash; a drift row has baseline_hash != target_hash, and sync_label is written only by TA-005.
state=off rows have target_path of the disabled item and no file on disk; state=linked rows have a target_path whose link or copy hash matches target_hash.
Every state change stores the operations id that caused it; last_verified_at updates on rescan even when state is unchanged.
Querying the full 3k items x 3 agents matrix for the skills screen returns in under 50 ms using the deployments(agent_id,scope) index.
notes: Field semantics: state is the observed deployment state, mode is how it is deployed. `off` is an explicit user intent stored in agent config, not a missing file.

title: DB schema: native_items, drift_events, locks
description: Migration v5. `native_items(id TEXT PK, agent_id TEXT, scope TEXT, kind TEXT, name TEXT, path TEXT UNIQUE, content_hash TEXT, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, adopted_item_id TEXT NULL, status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('new','adopted','ignored','missing')))`. `locks(id INTEGER PK, item_id TEXT, scope TEXT, reason TEXT, locked_by TEXT, locked_at, UNIQUE(item_id, scope))`. `drift_events(id INTEGER PK, item_id TEXT NULL, agent_id TEXT, scope TEXT, path TEXT, expected_hash TEXT, actual_hash TEXT, detected_at, resolved_at NULL, resolution TEXT NULL CHECK(resolution IN ('adopt','restore','ignore')), backup_id TEXT NULL)`. Indexes: native_items(agent_id, status), native_items(kind), native_items(last_seen_at), locks(item_id), drift_events(item_id, detected_at DESC), drift_events(resolved_at). Rebuildable: native_items and locks yes (scan and store lock files); drift_events no, it is history that survives rescan.
acceptance: Scanning a native folder inserts one row per discovered item; a second scan with unchanged content updates last_seen_at only, and a vanished item becomes status=missing rather than being deleted.
Adopting a native item sets adopted_item_id to the new canonical item and status=adopted while preserving the original path and first_seen_at.
locks is unique per (item_id, scope); a Global lock row makes a resolution query return locked=true for lower scopes.
Resolving a drift event sets resolved_at and resolution; unresolved events for an item are returned newest-first in under 10 ms with 100k history rows.
Deleting a canonical item does not delete native_items rows; it sets nothing and leaves the native row pointing to a missing adopted_item_id only when the delete is forced (rare, admin).
notes: drift_events is retained by TF-050. Locks are mirrored to store lock files so a rebuild can reconstruct intent.

title: DB schema: health_checks, sources
description: Migration v6. `health_checks(id INTEGER PK, item_id TEXT NULL, scope TEXT, project_id TEXT NULL, agent_id TEXT, server_name TEXT, transport TEXT CHECK(transport IN ('stdio','http','sse')), checked_at, status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('ok','failed','unknown','skipped_offline')), trigger TEXT CHECK(trigger IN ('manual','scheduled','startup')), latency_ms INTEGER, tools_count INTEGER, error_code TEXT, error_text_redacted TEXT)`. `sources(id TEXT PK, item_id TEXT NULL REFERENCES items(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, kind TEXT CHECK(kind IN ('git','library','local','folder','marketplace','zip')), url TEXT, subpath TEXT, commit_sha TEXT, git_ref TEXT, version TEXT, content_hash TEXT, marketplace_id TEXT, install_count INTEGER, etag TEXT, remote_sha TEXT, ignored_sha TEXT, local_modified INTEGER, auto_update INTEGER, deleted_at, installed_at, last_checked_at, update_available INTEGER, license TEXT)`. Indexes: health_checks(item_id, checked_at DESC), health_checks(checked_at), health_checks(server_name, checked_at DESC), health_checks(status), sources(item_id), sources(url), sources(kind), sources(marketplace_id), sources(deleted_at). Rebuildable: sources yes from store source metadata; health_checks no, it is history owned by TM-009 retention.
acceptance: Latest health per server query uses (item_id, checked_at DESC) and returns one row per server in under 10 ms with 100k history rows.

A failed check stores error_code plus error_text_redacted and tools_count NULL; an ok check stores latency_ms and tools_count; a skipped_offline check stores NULL latency, NULL tools_count and no error.
error_text_redacted never contains a value from secret_refs or an env assignment pattern (redaction test with a sentinel token).

A git source stores url, subpath, commit_sha and remote_sha; a folder source stores a path with kind=folder; a marketplace source stores marketplace_id and install_count; etag, ignored_sha, local_modified and auto_update default NULL/0, and a soft delete sets deleted_at while content_hash remains.
Inserting status='timeout' or trigger='cron' fails the CHECK constraint; transport accepts stdio, http and sse only.
notes: Health writes come from the MCP slice; this story only guarantees the storage contract and query shape.

title: DB schema: operations, operation_files, backups
description: Migration v7. `operations(id TEXT PK, kind TEXT, scope TEXT, actor TEXT, status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('running','succeeded','failed','interrupted','undone')), summary TEXT, error_kind TEXT, started_at, finished_at, correlation_id TEXT, undo_of TEXT NULL)`. `operation_files(id INTEGER PK, operation_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, path TEXT, action TEXT CHECK(action IN ('created','modified','deleted','linked','moved')), before_hash TEXT, after_hash TEXT, backup_id TEXT NULL, bytes_before INTEGER, bytes_after INTEGER)`. `backups(id TEXT PK, operation_id TEXT NULL, original_path TEXT, backup_path TEXT UNIQUE, content_hash TEXT, size INTEGER, created_at, pinned INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, expires_at, restore_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)`. Indexes: operations(started_at DESC), operations(kind, status), operations(correlation_id), operation_files(operation_id), operation_files(path), backups(original_path, created_at DESC), backups(expires_at), backups(content_hash). Rebuildable: none of the three; history and the backup catalogue are the only non-rebuildable state in at-db, so the database file itself is backed up on a schedule and before migrations.
acceptance: A single apply removes one operation and its files in one transaction; a failed insert rolls back both tables.
Deleting an operations row cascades operation_files but no public API exposes deletion; operation count only grows.
Backups lookup by original_path returns newest first and includes a pinned boolean and expires_at; backup_path is unique globally.
operation_files.action='linked' stores before_hash NULL and after_hash equal to the canonical content hash.
The schema test asserts operations and backups have no updated_at column and no delete triggers.
notes: Write API is TF-009, backup lifecycle TF-041 and TF-050. Non-rebuildable state is protected by TF-020.

title: DB schema: presets, preset_members, preset_applications
description: Migration v8. `presets(id TEXT PK, name TEXT, description TEXT, scope TEXT, is_builtin INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at, updated_at, UNIQUE(name, scope COLLATE NOCASE))`. `preset_members(id INTEGER PK, preset_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES presets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, item_id TEXT, kind TEXT, enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, UNIQUE(preset_id, item_id))`. `preset_applications(id INTEGER PK, preset_id TEXT NOT NULL, target_kind TEXT CHECK(target_kind IN ('agent','project')), target_id TEXT, applied_at, operation_id TEXT, member_count INTEGER)`. `preset_application_members(id INTEGER PK, application_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES preset_applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, item_id TEXT NOT NULL, prior_enabled INTEGER, UNIQUE(application_id, item_id))`. Indexes: preset_members(preset_id), preset_applications(preset_id), preset_applications(target_kind, target_id), preset_application_members(application_id). Rebuildable: presets and preset_members yes from presets.json; preset_applications and preset_application_members no, they are history.
acceptance: Two presets may share a name in different scopes, but `Frontend` and `frontend` in the same scope fail UNIQUE(name, scope).
Deleting a preset cascades preset_members and leaves preset_applications and preset_application_members history intact.
preset_members is unique per (preset_id,item_id); enabled=0 is an explicit opt-out and survives round-trip.
Applying a preset writes one preset_applications row and one preset_application_members row per member with prior_enabled equal to the state before apply.
A rebuild from presets.json reproduces presets and members but preserves, not recreates, preset_applications and preset_application_members.
notes: Presets file format is owned by the skills slice; this story fixes the DB mirror.

title: DB schema: settings, secret_refs, remote_backup_state
description: Migration v9. `settings(key TEXT PK, value_json TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at)`. `secret_refs(name TEXT PK, keychain_service TEXT, account TEXT, created_at, rotated_at, last_read_ok_at)`. `secret_ref_uses(id INTEGER PK, secret_name TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES secret_refs(name) ON DELETE CASCADE, item_id TEXT NULL, scope TEXT, UNIQUE(secret_name, item_id, scope))`. `remote_backup_state(id INTEGER PK CHECK(id = 1), repo_url TEXT, branch TEXT, last_push_at, last_pull_at, last_commit TEXT, status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('unconfigured','idle','syncing','error')), error_kind TEXT)`. Indexes: secret_ref_uses(secret_name), secret_ref_uses(item_id), settings(updated_at). The schema test asserts secret_refs and secret_ref_uses have no column capable of holding a secret value. Rebuildable: secret_refs and secret_ref_uses yes from ${VAR} references found in store files plus a Keychain existence probe; remote_backup_state yes from the configured repo; settings no, the DB is authoritative and exported as JSON only for CLI parity. No note column exists; TM-010 will not add one.
acceptance: `PRAGMA table_info(secret_refs)` lists name, keychain_service, account, created_at, rotated_at and last_read_ok_at only, with no note column; a schema test fails if any other column matches /value|token|password|note/.
secret_refs.name is the primary key; inserting the same name twice fails. secret_ref_uses is unique per (secret_name,item_id,scope), and deleting a secret_ref cascades its uses.
remote_backup_state rejects a second row (CHECK id=1) and starts with status=unconfigured.

Scanning store files for ${VAR} creates one secret_refs row per unique name and one secret_ref_uses row per (item, scope); removing the last use deletes the use row and keeps the ref while the Keychain item exists.
last_read_ok_at updates on a successful Keychain read and rotated_at on rotation; neither stores a value, and settings values round-trip byte-identically.
notes: Secret values live only in Keychain (at-secrets, TM slice); this slice guarantees the DB cannot hold them.

title: DB rebuild and reindex from files
description: Implement `at-db::rebuild`: regenerate all derived tables from disk in one resumable job: projects, agents, agent_paths, items, item_versions, native_items, deployments, locks, sources, presets, preset_members, secret_refs, secret_ref_uses, remote_backup_state. Preserve history tables: operations, operation_files, backups, health_checks, drift_events, preset_applications, preset_application_members, settings. Steps: snapshot counts, mark job running in settings (key rebuild.state), delete derived rows inside a transaction, scan stores and agent folders via at-store/at-adapters, insert rows, verify invariants (every linked deployment points to an existing item and target), emit progress events through TF-008, rollback on scan error. Expose CLI-equivalent `RebuildReport { counts, duration_ms, warnings }` and a DB-only mode that skips UI.
acceptance: A fixture with 3 scopes, 40 items, 3 agents and grown history rebuilds from an empty derived state to a normalized dump identical to a cold full scan, ignoring timestamps.
History row counts for operations, operation_files, backups, health_checks, drift_events, preset_applications, preset_application_members and settings are identical before and after a rebuild.
Deleting agentuna.db and rebuilding 3k items completes in under 2 s and the UI shows progress with no frame over 32 ms.
A file deleted from disk disappears from items, item_versions and deployments; a new native SKILL.md appears as native_items with status=new.
Rebuild is idempotent: two consecutive runs produce an identical normalized dump and no duplicate rows; an aborted rebuild leaves the previous derived data intact.
notes: This is the recovery path when the index disagrees with disk. History preservation is the hard requirement.

title: DB startup integrity check, schema-version guard, backup-before-migrate
description: On every app start and before any migration: run `PRAGMA quick_check` (full integrity_check on last unclean shutdown), verify schema_version checksums, and reject schema versions newer than the binary. Before applying pending migrations, copy the database file to backups/db/agentuna-<version>-<timestamp>.db with fsync, keep the three newest copies, and delete older ones only after the migration commits. On corruption: rename the live file to agentuna.db.corrupt-<timestamp>, create a fresh database, rebuild derived tables (TF-019), and surface a non-blocking warning with the quarantine path. On clean shutdown run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and `PRAGMA optimize`.
acceptance: A hand-corrupted database file fails quick_check, is moved to agentuna.db.corrupt-<ts>, a new database is created, and the app starts with derived data rebuilt and a warning carrying the quarantine path.
A pending migration creates one db backup first; migration failure restores the backup and leaves the original schema_version unchanged.
A database reporting schema_version 999 fails startup with SchemaTooNew before any write; the file mtime and bytes are unchanged.
The backup directory keeps exactly the three newest pre-migration copies; older ones are deleted only after success.
Clean shutdown leaves no -wal file larger than 0 bytes and the next startup does not run recovery.
notes: Protects the only non-rebuildable state (history and backup catalogue) from migration accidents.

title: DB shared row structs and deployment matrix query
description: Provide only the cross-slice DB shared surface: row structs used by all list screens (ItemRow, ProjectRef, AgentRef, DeploymentCell, DeploymentMatrixRow, BackupRow, OperationRow) with serde Serialize/Deserialize and stable field names, plus deployment_matrix(item_ids, agent_ids, scope, project_id) -> Vec<DeploymentMatrixRow>. Domain list queries do not live here: skills lists belong to TS-001, MCP lists to TM-033, agent/effective lists to TA-042; they depend on these structs. Queries use one prepared statement, no SELECT *, and return explicit rows.
acceptance: deployment_matrix for 3k items x 3 agents x 3 scopes returns one cell per pair in under 50 ms and includes state, mode, store_hash, target_hash, baseline_hash and sync_label.
Row structs serialize to stable snake_case JSON; a snapshot test fails on a renamed field, and each struct is constructible from a DB row without rusqlite types leaking.
No domain list query (skills_list, mcp_list, effective_rows) exists in at-db; a grep/test asserts those symbols live in the TS/TM/TA repositories.
A statement-count hook asserts exactly one query per deployment_matrix call, a reused prepared statement across calls, and no N+1 query per agent.
NULL project_id is normalized to the empty sentinel in matrix keys so Global/User rows match exactly one cell.
notes: Decision 8: DDL stays in TF, but domain list queries move to TS-001, TM-033 and TA-042. This story keeps only shared structs and the matrix.

title: App path resolution (directories crate)
description: Implement AppPaths as the single source of every filesystem root, using the directories crate plus explicit overrides. macOS: support dir from ProjectDirs (Application Support), with db at <support>/agentuna.db, logs/, backups/ and cache/ beneath it; user store at ~/.agentuna; project store at <projectRoot>/.agentuna; global store default at `/Library/Application Support/AgenTuna/global`. Global store resolution order is env `AGENTUNA_GLOBAL_STORE`, then settings key `global_store_path`, then the default; because settings open after the DB, AppPaths resolves defaults first and applies the settings override in a second pass. Other overrides: AGENTUNA_HOME (support), AGENTUNA_USER_STORE, AGENTUNA_PROJECT_STORE. Create user store 0700, project store 0755, cache 0700. Every crate receives &AppPaths; no module may call dirs::home_dir directly (enforced by a grep test). Missing HOME returns PathError::HomeUnavailable instead of panicking.
acceptance: A macOS unit test snapshots support, db, log, backup, cache, user-store, project-store and global-store paths; the global default is `/Library/Application Support/AgenTuna/global`.
AGENTUNA_HOME relocates db, logs, backups and cache beneath it and wins over ProjectDirs.
Global store resolution is AGENTUNA_GLOBAL_STORE, then settings key global_store_path, then the documented default; the second AppPaths pass applies the settings value once the DB is open.
Missing HOME or a missing project root returns typed PathError values, never panics; project store requires an existing project path and created dirs have modes 0700/0755.
A grep test fails if crates other than at-store/at-app call dirs::home_dir, std::env::var("HOME") or construct .agentuna literally.
notes: Decision 2: default and override order are fixed here. Decision 3: user store mirrors the project layout minus local/.

title: Settings storage and typed preferences
description: Implement typed Settings over the settings table: one row per key with a versioned JSON payload. Canonical keys and defaults: health_interval_minutes (allowed 0,5,15,60; default 5, 0=off), background_health (off|local|all; default local), backup_retention_days (integer, clamped to min 30), default_link_mode (link|copy), link_mode.<agent> (link|copy per agent id), native_banner_hidden.<kind> (bool per item kind), global_store_path (absolute path or empty), network.marketplace_enabled (bool, default false), auto_update_skills (bool, default false), last_scope.<project_id> (global|user|project|local, default empty), last_project_id (project id or empty). Export `UNDO_WINDOW_DAYS: u32 = 30` used by undo and retention; it is a constant, not a setting. Settings struct has schema_version; unknown stored keys are preserved and invalid values fall back to the default with a warning. get/set are transactional; changes to audit-sensitive keys emit an operations row of kind Settings.
acceptance: Every canonical key returns its documented default when absent, including auto_update_skills=false, last_project_id empty and last_scope.<project_id> empty; a fresh database reads a complete, valid Settings without writing rows.
health_interval_minutes accepts only 0,5,15,60 and rejects 7 or 30; background_health accepts only off, local or all.

backup_retention_days below 30 is clamped to 30 with a warning; link_mode.<agent> and native_banner_hidden.<kind> accept only known agent ids and item kinds; last_scope.<project_id> accepts only global, user, project or local.
UNDO_WINDOW_DAYS equals 30 and a test asserts it is a const with no settings row or override; undo expiry and backup retention read it.
Export then import into an empty database round-trips all keys byte-identically; an import with one invalid key writes nothing and reports the key.
notes: Decision 9 plus decision 18: this key list is canonical; TU-019 Preferences edits these values. health_checks retention is TM-009 and is not a setting. The per-agent link key is link_mode.<agent> only.

title: Logging and tracing setup with redaction
description: Initialize tracing in at-app and at-cli: EnvFilter from RUST_LOG or Settings.log_level (default info), a daily rolling file appender at <logs>/agentuna-YYYY-MM-DD.log with 30-day retention, compact text by default and JSON when AGENTUNA_LOG_JSON=1. Include fields: app version, session id, operation id, job id, agent id, path (relative to home when possible). Install tracing_panic for panics. Add a redaction layer that replaces known secret values from at-secrets and env-assignment shapes (NAME=value, Bearer tokens, ghp_, sk-) with `***`, while leaving `${VAR}` references literal. Log file open failure falls back to stderr. Never log file contents, secret values, full config dumps or clipboard text.
acceptance: First run creates <logs>/agentuna-YYYY-MM-DD.log containing one startup line with app version, macOS version and schema version.
A log call containing a known Keychain secret value or `GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_x` emits `***` for the value and the literal string `${GITHUB_TOKEN}` is never altered.
Changing log_level at runtime takes effect within one second through a reload handle, without restart.
Log files older than 30 days are deleted on startup; a read-only log directory falls back to stderr and the app still starts.
A panic inside a job writes one ERROR entry with panic message, job id and backtrace location, then the process continues.
notes: Redaction utility is TF-045; this story wires it into the subscriber. Diagnostics export is TF-025.

title: Log viewer and diagnostics export
description: Implement `ui/src/screens/settings` log section: read the newest log file tail (last 1000 lines), show level filter (ERROR/WARN/INFO/DEBUG/TRACE), module filter and substring search; a Reveal in Finder button; and Export diagnostics. The export writes a zip via a temp file + atomic rename containing: logs/app.log (redacted), diagnostics.json (app version, OS, schema version, agent detection summary with paths/formats/counts, effective settings, feature flags, db integrity result), and schema.txt. Never include item contents, file diffs, Keychain values or env values. Export has no network. Screen states: empty (no log dir), loading (spinner), error (path + reason + Retry), populated (virtualized list with tail-follow toggle).
acceptance: Empty log directory renders an empty state with the resolved log path and no error toast.
Unreadable or missing current log file renders the error state with the path and a Retry button; Retry re-reads without restarting.
Filters combine: ERROR + module svc=fs + text `concurrent` shows only matching lines and the count of hidden lines.
Export produces a zip at the chosen path, readable by unzip -t, whose diagnostics.json parses and whose log text contains no secret sentinel planted in a secret_refs value.
Cancelling the save dialog leaves no temp or partial file; exporting to a read-only location shows PermissionDenied with the path.
notes: UI module name from CONTRACT.md: ui/src/screens/settings. Diagnostics bundle is the support path for privacy-preserving reports.

title: Error model and user-facing error mapping
description: Define `at-model::error` with ErrorReport { kind: ErrorKind, message: String, path: Option<PathBuf>, operation_id: Option<String>, source_chain: Vec<String>, remedy: Vec<Remedy>, retryable: bool } and ErrorKind: Io, PermissionDenied, NotFound, InvalidFormat, Conflict, ConcurrentModification, RefusedOverwrite, Locked, UnsupportedPlatform, Network, Auth, SecretMissing, UpdateSignatureInvalid, Internal, Cancelled. Each kind has a stable code (`E_PERMISSION_DENIED`, ...) used by CLI --json and logs. Implement From<io::Error>, From<serde_json::Error>, From<toml_edit::TomlError> in the owning crates, and Display that never emits only an OS string. Remedy: Adopt, MoveAside, Retry, OpenFolder, RevealInFinder, Reauthenticate, InstallAgent, SetPath, OpenSettings, CopyDetails, Cancel. at-app::app::state maps ErrorReport to a short user_message plus a Details drawer; at-cli prints code, message and remedy ids as JSON.
acceptance: Every ErrorKind round-trips its code and the code is unique; a snapshot test locks all 15 code strings.
std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied converts to PermissionDenied with the path populated and user_message `Cannot write <path> because the folder is read-only.`.
Display and Debug never panic on nested sources; Debug includes the source chain while user_message excludes it.
A RefusedOverwrite carries remedies [Adopt, MoveAside, Cancel] and the app renders exactly those actions for the error.
A sentinel secret value passed into any error path never appears in Display, user_message, logs or --json output.
notes: Conversions live in owning crates to keep at-model IO-free; at-app module app::state owns presentation. Details drawer pairs with TU toast/dialog.

title: Crash recovery and unclean-shutdown repair
description: Implement startup recovery: acquire the single-instance lock (TF-051), read session.json { pid, started_at, clean_exit }, and if the last exit was unclean: run db integrity (TF-020), scan cache/pending/*.journal for writes that began but never finished, mark those operations interrupted (TF-009), and collect temp files matching `*.agentuna-tmp-*`. Present a Recovery sheet with: interrupted operations and their files, Restore from backup per file, Discard pending, Continue. Restore runs through TF-004 with a Restore operation and backs up current bytes first. Remove temp and journal files only after the user chooses or after 7 days. If a pending journal names a file whose bytes match neither before nor after hash, report ManualReviewRequired and never auto-restore.
acceptance: A SIGKILL between backup and rename leaves one journal entry; next start shows exactly one interrupted operation with the affected path and offers Restore, which returns the file to its before_hash.
Choosing Discard removes the journal and temp files, leaves the original bytes untouched and keeps the interrupted operation row for audit.
A journal whose file hash matches neither before nor after is shown as ManualReviewRequired and no automatic write occurs.
A clean previous exit shows no recovery sheet; temp files older than 7 days are removed automatically while unrelated files in the same directories are untouched.
Recovery completes before the main window is interactive and reports duration in the log; a second instance cannot run recovery concurrently.
notes: Crash recovery is the user-visible promise behind atomic writes. ManualReviewRequired protects hand-edited files.

title: Runtime config and feature flags
description: Implement agentuna.toml in the support dir with [flags] marketplace=false, remote_backup=false, auto_update=false, instructions=true, presets=true, plus [advanced] values. Precedence: CLI --flag vendor:name=value > env AGENTUNA_FLAG_<NAME> > file > compiled default. Unknown keys warn once with a suggestion. Flags are read once at startup into a typed FeatureFlags struct and exposed read-only; changing a flag requires restart and the UI states that. Feature flags gate only new surfaces, never safety: allow_overwrite, skip_backup, disable_concurrency_check and disable_refuse_overwrite are rejected with a warning even if present. `agentuna config --json` and diagnostics export print effective flags with their source.
acceptance: On first run the file is created with comments and all defaults; deleting it restores defaults on next start.
Precedence is proven by four tests: default vs file vs env vs CLI, each returning the expected effective value and source label.
An unknown key logs one WARN with the key and a nearest-known suggestion; startup continues.
Setting allow_overwrite=true, skip_backup=true or disable_refuse_overwrite=true is ignored and logs `safety flag cannot be disabled`.
`agentuna config --json` output lists every flag with value, default and source; diagnostics.json contains the same object.
notes: Flags let unfinished surfaces ship dark without branching the codebase. Safety is not flaggable.

title: macOS .app bundle packaging
description: Add scripts/bundle.sh (plus a make target) that builds `cargo build --release -p at-app` for the host arch and assembles `AgenTuna.app`: Contents/Info.plist (CFBundleIdentifier com.agentuna.app, CFBundleName AgenTuna, CFBundleShortVersionString and CFBundleVersion from Cargo, LSMinimumSystemVersion 13.0, NSHighResolutionCapable true, CFBundleIconFile AppIcon, NSHumanReadableCopyright), Contents/MacOS/agentuna-app, Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns and fonts, Contents/Frameworks if needed. Strip the binary, set 0755 permissions, validate plist with plutil, and fail on missing icon, missing version or a non-system dylib outside /usr/lib and /System. Optional universal build via `--universal` (arm64 + x86_64 lipo).
acceptance: `scripts/bundle.sh` exits 0 and produces `target/release/AgenTuna.app`; `plutil -lint Contents/Info.plist` reports OK.
`open 'target/release/AgenTuna.app'` launches the app without a terminal and the window title matches the app name.
CFBundleShortVersionString equals the workspace version and CFBundleVersion is a monotonic integer; bumping Cargo.toml changes both after rebuild.
`otool -L` lists only system libraries and the binary is stripped; bundle size is under 60 MB.
Missing AppIcon.icns or an invalid plist makes the script exit non-zero with the offending path.
notes: Release engineering only; no runtime code. Signing is TF-031, DMG is TF-030.

title: DMG creation
description: Add scripts/dmg.sh using create-dmg (or hdiutil fallback): volume name `AgenTuna <version>`, layout with the app on the left and an Applications symlink on the right, background image, window size 640x400, icon positions, HFS+ UDBZ compression, output `dist/AgenTuna-<version>.dmg`, then codesign the dmg and write `dist/AgenTuna-<version>.dmg.sha256`. Refuse to build if the app bundle is unsigned or fails codesign --verify. The script is idempotent: existing output is replaced atomically.
acceptance: Mounting the dmg shows exactly `AgenTuna.app` and an Applications alias; dragging the app to Applications is possible.
`hdiutil verify` reports the image is valid and the sha256 file matches `shasum -a 256` output.
The volume name includes the version and the dmg file name is deterministic for a given version and arch.
Running the script with an unsigned app exits non-zero before creating an image.
Rebuilding the same version replaces the dmg and checksum without leaving temp images mounted.
notes: Notarization and stapling are applied before dmg signing in TF-031.

title: Code signing and notarization
description: Add release signing: entitlements.plist with com.apple.security.network.client true (MCP HTTP, git, updater), no JIT and no library-validation bypass; sign the inner binary first, then frameworks, then the app with Developer ID Application and --options runtime --timestamp; verify with codesign --verify --deep --strict and codesign -dv; submit with xcrun notarytool submit --wait using an app-specific password or API key from CI secrets; staple the app and dmg; verify with spctl -a -vv and `stapler validate`. Local builds without credentials use ad-hoc signing (`codesign -s -`) and the About box shows `Local build (unsigned)`. CI workflow requires SIGNING_IDENTITY, TEAM_ID, NOTARY_APPLE_ID, NOTARY_PASSWORD or API key, stored as repository secrets; missing secrets skip signing with a warning on non-release branches and fail on release tags.
acceptance: codesign -dv --verbose=4 on the release app reports Developer ID Application, hardened runtime and a secure timestamp.
codesign --verify --deep --strict and spctl -a -vv succeed on a stapled build; `stapler validate` succeeds on app and dmg.
notarytool reports status Accepted for the release artifact; a rejected submission fails the release job and prints the notary log URL.
A local build without credentials succeeds ad-hoc signed and the About box displays `Local build (unsigned)`.
Entitlements.plist snapshot contains exactly network.client and no allow-jit, allow-unsigned-executable-memory or disable-library-validation keys.
notes: Signed and notarized is an explicit trust signal in the product research. Secrets never enter the repo.

title: In-app updater with signature verification
description: Implement update checking in at-app as an explicit action only: a Check for Updates menu item, or automatic check only when Settings.update_check=automatic is chosen by the user; no background check on first launch. Manifest over HTTPS: { version, min_os, channel, url, sha256, notes_url, published_at, signature } where signature is Ed25519 over the canonical JSON of the manifest without the signature field. Embed the public key in the binary. Flow: fetch manifest, verify signature before parsing url fields, compare versions (honor channel stable/beta, reject downgrade unless allow_downgrade), download to cache/updates/<version>.zip, verify sha256, unzip to temp, verify codesign of the new app against the same Team ID, then install by replacing the app bundle via a small helper after the user confirms; if replacement fails, keep the old bundle and report UpdateInstallFailed. Never install during an active operation; wait for quiescence. Record check and install outcomes in operations with kind Update.
acceptance: A manifest with a tampered field or invalid signature returns UpdateSignatureInvalid and performs no download; the network layer records only the manifest GET.
A downloaded archive whose sha256 differs is deleted and reported UpdateChecksumMismatch; no unzip or install occurs.
A valid signed update replaces the bundle, relaunches the new version, and About shows the new version; the previous bundle is kept until first successful launch of the new one.
With update_check=manual and no user action, launching and idling 10 minutes performs zero outbound connections.
A version lower than the running version is rejected unless allow_downgrade=true; installing while a deploy operation is running is deferred with a queued state, never interlaced.
notes: Uses signature verification plus Apple code signing; both must pass. App updates are separate from skill update tracking (E14).

title: CI: macOS build, clippy, workspace tests
description: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml running on macos-14: checkout, install the pinned toolchain, cache ~/.cargo registry and target with Cargo.lock key, then `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and `cargo build --release -p at-app`. Set CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always, RUST_BACKTRACE=1 on failure, timeout 45 minutes, concurrency group per branch with cancel-in-progress. Upload test logs and any golden diff artifacts on failure. No secrets required for this job. Add actionlint to pre-commit and a branch-protection note in CONTRIBUTING.
acceptance: A pull request introducing an unused variable or a clippy lint fails the clippy step and reports the file and line.
A failing test fails the job and uploads the test log artifact even when earlier steps passed.
Cold-cache run completes in under 25 minutes and warm-cache run under 10 minutes on macos-14.
The workflow passes actionlint and contains no repository secrets; release signing is a separate workflow.
`cargo fmt --check` failing is reported separately from clippy so the fix is obvious.
notes: Required checks for merge. Golden job is TF-034.

title: CI golden-file verification job
description: Add a `golden` CI job and `scripts/golden.sh --check|--update|--diff` that runs the format-preservation suite (TF-046) offline with UPDATE_GOLDEN unset. The job regenerates output into a temp dir and compares byte-for-byte with tests/golden/**; on mismatch it writes unified diffs to target/golden-diff/ and uploads them as an artifact. `--update` rewrites expected files and must be committed deliberately. Keep a manifest of fixture sha256 so an accidental agent-format change is visible. The job runs in parallel with the main test job and needs no macOS GUI.
acceptance: An intentional whitespace or key-order change in an adapter output makes the job fail and the artifact contains a unified diff naming the fixture path and line.
`scripts/golden.sh --update` followed by `--check` passes and the diff is limited to expected files.
The job performs no network access and completes in under 3 minutes.
A missing golden file fails with `missing expected file` rather than silently creating it.
The golden manifest lists every fixture with sha256 and the job fails if a fixture is added without a manifest entry.
notes: Catches the highest-risk regression: rewriting an entire agent config because a patch was not span-preserving.

title: Performance budgets: startup, idle CPU, memory
description: Build a deterministic performance harness: seed a fixture database with 3k items, 9k deployments, 3 agents and 10k operation rows; launch a release build with `--perf-mode <scenario>` that records time-to-first-frame, time-to-interactive, RSS and CPU time samples; `scripts/perf.sh` runs the matrix and writes JSON plus a markdown table to BENCHMARK.md. Budgets on the M4 baseline: cold start under 1 s for 3k items, idle CPU under 1 percent averaged over 60 s, RSS under 250 MB, skills list first paint under 150 ms, scroll frame under 16 ms with 3k rows, watcher idle wakeups under 5 per second, and no webview re-render when no input or job event occurs. A regression over 20 percent vs the recorded baseline fails nightly CI; PR runs the quick scenario only.
acceptance: `scripts/perf.sh --quick` prints one line per budget with measured value, budget and pass/fail, and exits non-zero when any budget is exceeded.
Startup with the 3k-item fixture reports time-to-first-frame under 1000 ms on the M4 baseline and records the number in BENCHMARK.md.
Idle for 60 s with the window focused produces CPU time under 0.6 s and fewer than 300 watcher wakeups; the React Profiler records zero commits without events.
Scrolling the skills list with 3k rows keeps p95 frame time under 16 ms in release mode.
A synthetic regression (forced 500 ms sleep on startup) makes the nightly job fail with the budget name and values.
notes: Numbers are measured, not asserted: BENCHMARK.md holds raw results and the baseline commit. Idle CPU around 0 is a product promise from the design.

title: Privacy guarantee and network allow-list
description: Implement a single network policy in at-model: NetworkAction enum (GitFetch, GitClone, MarketplaceBrowse, MarketplaceInstall, UpdateCheck, UpdateDownload, RemoteBackupPush, RemoteBackupPull, McpRemoteConnect, McpOAuth, ScheduledHttpHealthCheck) with a user-facing label and an `explicit` flag. A pure NetworkPolicy::permits(action, host) decides; no IO in at-model. Enforce it at every egress site: at-git shells out to git only inside a function that takes NetworkAction and logs the host; at-mcp connects HTTP only for a saved server or a user-triggered Test; at-app updater only after a user action or opt-in; marketplace only when opened. Deny by default: any egress call without a permitted action returns NetworkDenied before DNS. Add a Settings privacy section listing every action, its trigger and the last 20 network events (time, action, host, bytes) from a local ring buffer. ScheduledHttpHealthCheck is permitted only when Settings.background_health=all; scheduled stdio checks are local and use no network action. No analytics, no crash reporting, no auto-update without consent, no account.
acceptance: With default settings, launching the app, visiting every screen and idling 10 minutes produces zero DNS queries and zero outbound TCP connections, verified by an integration test that installs a process-wide socket and DNS hook plus a proxy recorder that logs every connection attempt, asserting zero attempts.
Calling any git, MCP HTTP or updater network function with no explicit action returns NetworkDenied and creates no socket; the unit test hooks connect() and asserts it is never called.

The NetworkAction registry contains exactly the 11 actions including ScheduledHttpHealthCheck; each has one label and one trigger, and permits() returns false for ScheduledHttpHealthCheck when background_health is off or local and true only when all.
A scheduled HTTP check with background_health=local is skipped without opening a socket and is stored with status skipped_offline; a stdio check needs no network action.
The local network event ring buffer stores at most 20 entries with no payload or header content, and clearing it is a button.
notes: X09 is a product promise; this story makes it architecture rather than intent. Secret redaction is TF-045.

title: Windows and Linux path portability
description: Remove macOS-only assumptions from path handling (phase later, after macOS MVP): AppPaths gains cfg(target_os) implementations using directories: Windows support dir %APPDATA%\AgenTuna, local state %LOCALAPPDATA%\AgenTuna, home %USERPROFILE%; Linux config ~/.config/agentuna, data ~/.local/share/agentuna, cache ~/.cache/agentuna, honoring XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME. Store paths in the DB with `/` separators via a PathKey newtype and convert at the boundary; never compare paths as strings on case-insensitive filesystems; handle long paths with `\?\` and avoid trailing dots/spaces. Agent path detection uses the same AppPaths abstraction. Add cross-compile checks (`cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) to CI as allowed-to-fail until the port phase.
acceptance: On macOS the full test suite still passes and no resolved path changes from the documented contract.
PathKey round-trips `C:\Users\a\.agentuna\skills\x` through DB storage and back to the platform-native path on Windows while the stored text uses forward slashes.
Linux path resolution honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME and falls back to ~/.config; Windows honors APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA; tests inject env roots and assert exact paths.
Path comparison is case-insensitive on macOS/Windows test doubles and case-sensitive on Linux, verified by a table-driven test.
Cross-compile checks pass for the two targets in a `portability` CI job marked continue-on-error until the phase is enabled.
notes: Phase later: post-MVP port, not part of the macOS first release. Marked to prevent hard-coded macOS assumptions now.

title: Windows junction fallback for directory links
description: Implement the Windows half of the deployment primitive (phase later): a Linker trait with symlink_dir, symlink_file, junction_dir, copy_dir. On Windows try CreateSymbolicLinkW; on ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD fall back to a directory junction (reparse point) when the setting allows, and to copy for files. Removal uses RemoveDirectory for junctions (never recurses into the target) and remove_file for symlinks. Validate that the resolved target is inside the AgenTuna store before removal. The junction fallback is recorded in deployments.mode as `junction` (extend the CHECK in a later migration).
acceptance: On Windows, link_dir for a directory creates a junction when the process lacks SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege; listing the junction shows the canonical store files.
Removing a junction removes only the reparse point; every canonical file hash is unchanged.
symlink_file falls back to copy when file symlinks are unavailable, and mode=copy with a manifest is recorded.
A shipped migration extends deployments.mode to accept junction; reading a junction row on macOS is rejected by the platform guard.
Windows-only tests are cfg-gated and compile on the CI portability job; macOS tests are unaffected.
notes: Phase later (Windows port). Needs a Windows CI runner before enabling. Junction creation does not require admin.

title: Linux desktop integration and XDG paths
description: Add Linux integration (phase later): install a .desktop entry with Name=AgenTuna, Exec=agentuna-app, Icon=agentuna, Categories=Development; install icons under hicolor; use XDG paths from TF-037; detect that no macOS Keychain exists and delegate to the at-secrets backend trait so Linux can use Secret Service when available, otherwise surface a clear unsupported message rather than writing plaintext secrets. Document package formats (AppImage or .deb) as follow-up. No hardcoded macOS APIs outside cfg(target_os = "macos").
acceptance: `desktop-file-validate agentuna.desktop` passes and the app appears in the desktop menu after install.
Exec launches the release binary and the app opens with XDG_CONFIG_HOME honoring the configured path.
On Linux without a Secret Service, saving an MCP secret returns SecretBackendUnavailable with no disk write; no plaintext fallback exists.
`cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` passes and macOS-only imports are all behind cfg.
The .desktop file and icons are installed by `scripts/install-linux.sh` and removed cleanly by its --uninstall path.
notes: Phase later. Secret backend work belongs to the secrets slice; this story only prevents an insecure fallback.

title: ChangeSet preview service (every write previewable)
description: Implement `at-engine::preview`: turn a planned set of file operations into Preview { files: Vec<FilePreview { path, action, before_hash, after_hash, diff: DiffKind, is_new, is_unmanaged, backup_required }>, totals, warnings, estimated_bytes } without touching disk. DiffKind is Unified { text, hunks } for text under 1 MB, Binary { size } for binary content, TooLarge { size } above 1 MB, and Unchanged. The preview reuses at-fs::diff and reads current bytes with O_NOFOLLOW. Warnings: unmanaged target, path outside expected root, file changed since plan, backup will fail. The preview is the only source the UI renders before Save in skill editor, MCP form, rules editor, migrate plan and drift resolution; apply takes the same ChangeSet plus a preview id, revalidates hashes, and goes through TF-053.
acceptance: Preview of a JSONC server edit shows exactly one hunk covering the changed property; all other bytes, comments and key order are untouched.
Binary fixture returns DiffKind::Binary with size and no diff bytes; a 2 MB text file returns TooLarge with size and no inline diff.
An unmanaged destination adds a warning `overwrite_refused` and the proposed content is still shown read-only.
Preview performs no writes: path mtime and hash are identical before and after, and no operations row is created.
Preview of 200 small files completes in under 300 ms and totals report count and bytes; applying with a stale preview id returns ConcurrentModification.
notes: S-039 is the contract: no write without a diff. TU-007 renders Unified diffs; this story produces them.

title: Backup copy primitive (copy, sidecar, hash verify)
description: Implement the low-level backup copy used by TF-004 and TF-053. `at-fs::backup::copy_into(operation_backup_dir, original_path, scope, relpath)` copies the current file bytes into a caller-supplied operation backup folder using temp+rename and fsync, then writes a `<name>.json` sidecar { original_path, content_hash, size, captured_at, scope, relpath }. The directory layout is owned by TC-014; this primitive never chooses a backups/ date layout, never writes a DB catalogue row, and never creates directories beyond the supplied operation folder. verify(backup_path, expected_hash) re-reads both blob and sidecar and returns BackupCorrupt on mismatch or missing sidecar. The caller records backups catalogue rows through TC-014.
acceptance: copy_into(operation_folder, original_path, scope, relpath) writes bytes identical to the source and a sidecar whose content_hash equals sha256 of the copy and of the original.
The blob is created with temp+rename and fsynced before the sidecar; re-running the same copy overwrites idempotently and leaves one blob plus one sidecar.
verify returns BackupCorrupt when the blob, sidecar hash or sidecar presence disagrees with expected_hash and leaves the live file untouched.
Permission denied or disk full during copy returns BackupFailed and leaves no partial file or sidecar in the operation folder.
The primitive never creates a directory outside the supplied operation folder and never writes inside the target file's directory.
notes: Decision 6: layout and catalogue are TC-014. This story is only the safe copy plus sidecar. TF-050 owns retention.

title: Overwrite refusal remedies: Move aside
description: Implement the remedy primitives used when TF-005 refuses a write: (1) move_aside(path) atomically renames the unmanaged file or directory to support/.moved-aside/<UTC timestamp>/<encoded absolute path>, records an operation with action moved and the inverse mapping, and returns MoveAsideOutcome { original, moved_to, operation_id }; (2) a RefusalRemedies value listing AdoptVia { flow_id: TC-011 }, MoveAside and Cancel. TF-042 implements no adopt logic: the Adopt button routes to the TC-011 adopt flow, which owns copying, id assignment and linking. Both primitives are reversible by operation id, and move_aside refuses cross-device moves without copy+delete verification.
acceptance: Given an unmanaged directory, move_aside moves the whole tree atomically within the same volume and returns the new path plus operation id; undo moves it back to the original path.
Cross-volume move (EXDEV) copies, verifies hashes, then deletes the source; an interrupted copy leaves the source untouched.
A read-only volume returns PermissionDenied and the disk state is byte-identical; every move writes an operations row with its inverse.
RefusalRemedies exposes AdoptVia { flow_id: TC-011 }, MoveAside and Cancel; the at-fs crate writes no adopt bytes.
A grep test asserts at-fs has no adopt_item symbol, and the Adopt action handler resolves to the TC-011 flow id.
notes: Decision 12: Adopt is owned by TC-011. TF-042 keeps refusal remedies and move_aside only.

title: Overwrite refusal dialog (Adopt, Move aside, Cancel)
description: Implement `ui/src/overlays/dialogs` overwrite refusal dialog. States: Refused (path, kind, existing hash, remedies), Working (Adopt or Move aside in progress with cancel disabled), Done (result summary plus Undo toast), Error (ErrorReport with Retry). Content: absolute path with copy button, sentence explaining AgenTuna will not overwrite an unmanaged file, primary Adopt, secondary Move aside, destructive styling only on Move aside, Cancel default, Esc cancels. The dialog is modal, traps focus, restores focus on close, and supports keyboard-only use. Long paths wrap and the middle of the path is preserved when truncating.
acceptance: Given RefusedOverwrite for a file and a directory, the dialog shows the absolute path, the kind-specific sentence and exactly Adopt, Move aside and Cancel actions.
Choosing Adopt runs the job with a spinner, disables repeated clicks, and on success shows the new store item and a toast with Undo.
Choosing Move aside shows the new path in the result and Undo restores the original path and hash.
Esc, Cancel and window close leave disk state identical (hash check before/after) and no operations row.
Keyboard tab order is Adopt, Move aside, Cancel; screen reader labels include the path; a 300-character path wraps without clipping.
notes: UI module follows CONTRACT.md ui/src/overlays/dialogs. Modal framework is TU-004; toast is TU-005.

title: Safety audit: every write path goes through the pipeline
description: Add an architectural guard plus an exhaustive integration test. Guard: clippy.toml `disallowed-methods` for std::fs::write, std::fs::OpenOptions with write/truncate, std::fs::rename and std::fs::remove_file outside at-fs; a grep test lists every allow attribute with a one-line justification. Integration matrix: enumerate public write entry points (skill create/edit/delete, MCP add/edit/delete, rule save, deploy/undeploy, migration apply, adopt, restore, settings import, preset apply) and for each assert: preview exists, backup row exists for modified files, one operation row, final hash matches, and undo list is complete. Property test: 100 random sequences of external writes and AgenTuna writes never leave a file with bytes that are neither the old nor the new version.
acceptance: `cargo clippy` fails when std::fs::write or File::create is used outside at-fs; every allow has a justification comment and the test lists them.
For every entry point in the matrix on an existing file, exactly one operation row and at least one backup row exist and after_hash equals sha256 of the file.
Creating a new file produces an operation row and zero backup rows; deleting a file produces a backup of the deleted content.
Injected external write between preview and apply yields ConcurrentModification and the external bytes remain intact.
Property test of 100 random interleavings leaves every file equal to one of the two known byte sequences; no partial or empty file is ever observed.
notes: This is the enforcement story for X06/X07. It also protects against future contributors adding a direct fs write.

title: Secret redaction utility
description: Implement `at-model::redact::Redactor` (pure, no IO): constructed with a set of known secret values and names from at-secrets; methods redact_text, redact_json, contains_secret. Rules: replace exact known values of length 6 or more with `***`; replace env assignment `NAME=value` when NAME matches a secret_ref name; replace bearer tokens (Bearer <token>), ghp_, gho_, sk-, xoxb-, AKIA patterns; never alter `${VAR}` references, `${VAR:-default}` syntax, or the secret name alone. Bounded time O(n) with a single scan and no regex backtracking risk. Used by TF-024 logging, TF-026 errors, TF-025 diagnostics export and preview warnings. A developer-mode diagnostic can list secret names but never values.
acceptance: A text containing a known secret value and the literal `${GITHUB_TOKEN}` yields `***` for the value and leaves `${GITHUB_TOKEN}` unchanged.
Twenty token shapes (ghp_, sk-, Bearer, AKIA, xoxb-, JWT) are redacted in a table-driven test while ordinary words of 6+ letters are not.
Values shorter than 6 characters are redacted only when the full env assignment form is present, avoiding mass false positives.
Redaction of a 10 MB string completes in under 50 ms and never panics on invalid UTF-8 boundaries (input is &str so bytes are valid).
A test asserts redact_text is applied on every export/log path by scanning the diagnostics bundle and log output for a sentinel secret value.
notes: No secret value ever enters at-model except through this explicit constructor. The secrets slice owns Keychain IO.

title: Golden-file round-trip harness for TOML/JSON
description: Create the format-preservation corpus and runner used by adapters. Fixtures under at-adapters/tests/fixtures: Claude `~/.claude.json` with nested mcpServers, comments, 2-space indent, unicode keys and a 5 MB variant; `.mcp.json`; `.claude/settings.local.json` with trailing commas where the parser allows; Codex `config.toml` with comments, blank lines, inline tables, dotted keys and custom key order; omp `mcp.json`; Cursor mcp.json. Cases: add server, edit server env, remove server, add skill link, remove skill link, no-op. For each case copy the fixture, apply the adapter patch, compare byte-for-byte to expected output under tests/golden/<case>/expected (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 regenerates), then reparse and compare semantic models. Assert that an edit changes only the targeted span by checking unchanged byte ranges and total length delta.
acceptance: Twelve cases pass byte-for-byte; `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p at-adapters --test golden` rewrites expected files and a clean run then passes.
For the add-server case the byte length delta equals the inserted text length and every byte before the insertion point is unchanged.
TOML edits preserve comments, blank lines and key order outside the edited table; JSONC edits preserve comments and trailing commas.
CRLF fixtures stay CRLF and a 5 MB `~/.claude.json` completes in under 200 ms.
A failure prints case id, fixture path and a unified diff; the suite runs offline in under 10 seconds.
notes: JSON patching uses jsonc-parser CST spans and TOML uses toml_edit; re-serializing a whole file is a failure. CI wiring is TF-034.

title: Scope resolution matrix fixture and runner
