description: Add a table-driven scope resolution suite under at-engine/tests: cases stored as JSON, each with a store fixture description (Global, User, Project, Local copies of skills/rules/MCP entries, lock files, disable lists, same-name skills, malformed entries, missing agent paths, custom agent) and expected output (effective rows with winning scope, shadowed set, locked flags, disabled-here rows, why-trace steps). The runner materializes the fixture via TF-010, invokes the engine resolution API, serializes the result deterministically and diffs against expected. Adding a case must require no Rust code. Cases cover precedence, lock blocking, disable-inherited writing only the project file, local gitignored overrides, shadowing by name and MCP id, and missing scope directories.
acceptance: Twenty-five cases run in under 5 seconds and each prints its id; a mismatch shows the field path and expected vs actual value.
Cases prove Global < User < Project < Local precedence for the same skill and the same MCP id, with the winning scope recorded in the why-trace.
A Global lock on an item makes every lower-scope case report locked=true and resolution still returns the Global value.
Disable-inherited for a project writes exactly one disable entry to the project config file and leaves the User definition byte-identical.
Adding a new JSON case file is picked up automatically; an invalid case file fails with its path and schema error.
notes: Matrix data is the source of truth for E01; no engine implementation is included here. Fixtures avoid real home paths.

title: Migration undo test fixtures and round-trip harness
description: Build fixtures and a runner for migration safety: a home with native skills and MCP entries in Claude Code, Codex and omp folders; a project with duplicate skill names and conflicting content; symlink and copy modes. The harness snapshots the full tree (paths, modes, symlink targets, hashes), runs scan -> plan -> dry run -> apply through at-migrate, asserts dry run wrote nothing, then runs undo and compares the snapshot. Cases: successful undo inside 30 days, undo after an external edit (must refuse with conflict), undo after 31 days (must refuse with expiry), apply failure midway (must roll back via backups), and undo idempotency.
acceptance: Dry run leaves the tree snapshot byte-identical while reporting the exact file list that apply would touch.
Scan, apply, undo restores the original tree snapshot including symlink targets and file modes within the test.
Undo after an external edit to a migrated file refuses with a conflict naming the path and leaves the edited file unchanged.
Undo after the 30-day window refuses with MigrationExpired and lists affected paths; no partial restore occurs.
An injected failure during apply rolls back all files to the pre-apply snapshot and leaves no dangling links or deployment rows.
notes: Migration implementation is TC-009/TC-010; this story owns the acceptance fixtures and invariant checks.

title: Fault injection: external writer race, permission denied, disk full, unsupported symlink
description: Add a failpoint layer (trait-based, compiled out in release) to at-fs and at-db plus a table-driven integration suite. Scenarios: (1) external writer modifies the destination between read and rename; (2) EACCES creating the temp file; (3) ENOSPC during write and during fsync; (4) EPERM on symlink creation; (5) EXDEV on rename for a link; (6) SIGKILL between backup and rename; (7) disk full while writing a backup; (8) read-only destination volume. Each scenario asserts the typed error kind, whether a backup exists, that the original bytes are unchanged or the new bytes are complete, that no temp files remain, and that the operation row is failed rather than succeeded. Recovery for the kill scenarios is verified on the next app start via TF-027.
acceptance: Eight scenarios pass and each asserts a specific ErrorKind and that the destination is either the exact old bytes or the exact new bytes, never partial.
Every failed scenario leaves zero files matching `*.agentuna-tmp-*` in the destination directory.
Disk full during backup aborts before the destination is opened for writing and returns BackupFailed.
The kill scenarios leave one interrupted operation and recovery restores the before_hash; the same test run passes twice in a row.
Suite runtime is under 30 seconds and failpoints are absent from release builds (cargo tree shows no fail dependency in the release profile).
notes: Failpoints are test-only and must not add branch cost to release builds.

title: DB retention and pruning
description: Implement housekeeping owned by TF-050: prune drift_events resolved older than 90 days; prune backups only when older than max(30, backup_retention_days) days AND not among the newest 3 for the same original_path AND not pinned; prune operations and operation_files older than 365 days except those referenced by pinned backups or within the 30-day UNDO_WINDOW_DAYS; mark native_items missing older than 90 days; delete log files older than 30 days. Health-check retention is owned by TM-009 (last 200 rows per server, pruned hourly) and is not touched here. Delete in batches of 500 rows in separate transactions, report per-table counts, run VACUUM only when free pages exceed 20 percent, and never prune during an active operation.
acceptance: Backups: a 29-day-old backup survives; a 31-day-old backup among the newest 3 for its original_path survives; a 31-day-old backup outside the newest 3 is pruned; a pinned 400-day-old backup survives.
Drift events resolved 89 days ago survive and those resolved 91 days ago are deleted; unresolved events are never pruned.
Undo of a 29-day-old operation works after pruning; undo at 31 days fails with UndoExpired (UNDO_WINDOW_DAYS = 30).
health_checks rows are unchanged by TF-050 even when older than 30 days; a test asserts the row count is identical before and after a pruning run (TM-009 owns health retention).
Pruning runs in 500-row batches with no single transaction over 100 ms, reports per-table counts, and defers while an operation is active.
notes: Decision 6 plus decision 19: TF-050 is the only backup-pruning implementation and test; TC-014 owns layout and catalogue. Addendum 11: health_checks retention belongs to TM-009 and is removed here.

title: Single-instance advisory lock and CLI coexistence
description: Implement an advisory lock with fs4 on <support>/instance.lock containing JSON { pid, version, started_at, mode }. App startup takes an exclusive lock; if held by a live process, the second instance activates the existing window (NSApplication activate / distributed notification) and exits 0 without opening a second window. Stale locks are detected by reading pid and start time and checking the process; stale file is replaced. CLI commands take a shared lock for reads and an exclusive lock per write transaction, cooperating with the app through the DB busy timeout. A `--read-only` mode opens SQLite with query_only=1 and never migrates. Release the lock on clean exit; never delete another instance's lock.
acceptance: Starting the app twice results in one process with one window; the second invocation exits 0 after focusing the first, within 500 ms.
A stale lock from a killed pid (same pid reused check via started_at) is reclaimed and startup proceeds; a live pid is never stolen.
A CLI write while the app is idle succeeds serially; a CLI write during a long migration waits or returns Busy with the lock holder pid and version.
The lock file contains pid, version, started_at and mode, and is valid JSON; a corrupt lock file is quarantined rather than causing a crash.
Read-only mode never writes, never migrates, and can run concurrently with the app; attempted writes return ReadOnly.
notes: Prevents two writers on the same store and DB. The CLI surface is owned by the CLI slice; this story supplies the lock.

title: ChangeSet and FileOp domain types
description: Add the pure types every multi-file write shares. FileOp enum: Write { path, bytes, expected: ExpectedState, follow_symlink, backup }, Delete { path, expected }, Symlink { link_path, target, mode }, Copy { source, dest, expected }, Move { from, to, expected }, Mkdir { path, mode, parents }. ExpectedState: Absent, Hash(String), HashAndMtime { hash, mtime }. ChangeSet { id, preview_id, operation_kind: OperationKind, scope, project_id, summary, ops: Vec<FileOp>, created_at } with validation: at least one op, unique destination paths, and no op targeting a parent directory of another. All types serialize stably for journals (TF-053). No IO in at-model.
acceptance: A ChangeSet with duplicate destination paths or with one op targeting a parent directory of another returns ChangeSetError::PathCollision before any IO.
FileOp variants Write, Delete, Symlink, Copy, Move and Mkdir round-trip serde JSON with stable tag names used by journals; an unknown variant fails with the offending field path.
ExpectedState::Absent, Hash and HashAndMtime round-trip; Hash rejects non-hex or wrong-length values.
An empty ChangeSet is rejected; operation_kind accepts all 26 OperationKind variants used by TF-009 and rejects unknown strings.
at-model remains IO-free: the crate compiles without tokio, rusqlite or std::fs, asserted by the dependency test.
notes: Decision 5: types live here; application is TF-053. preview_id links a ChangeSet to TF-040.

title: Journaled multi-file ChangeSet apply with rollback
description: Implement `at-fs::changeset::apply(ChangeSet, apply_context) -> ApplyOutcome`. Order: validate the set, open an operation via TF-009, take the store advisory lock, write and fsync `.state/journal/<operation_id>.json` containing the full op list and expected states, then for each FileOp: create a backup copy through TF-041 into the caller-supplied operation backup folder (TC-014 layout), apply atomically per TF-004 (or the link, copy, mkdir, move and delete primitives), and append a journal progress record after each completed op. On any failure, stop and roll back every completed op in reverse order using backups and recorded prior state; if rollback itself fails, keep the journal and mark the operation failed with manual review required. On success, write a committed marker, fsync, remove the journal, finish the operation. On startup, an uncommitted journal is rolled back, or completed when every op is recorded done, before the UI is interactive, coordinated with TF-027.
acceptance: A 5-file ChangeSet applies all ops and produces exactly one operation with 5 operation_files rows and a backup per modified or deleted file; each after_hash matches disk.
An injected failure on op 3 of 5 rolls back ops 1-2 to their before_hashes, leaves ops 4-5 untouched, writes no partial file, and records status=failed.

Journals live under `.state/journal/` relative to the active store, are fsynced before the first write, and contain the operation id and every op with expected state; a journal from an older schema version is rejected with JournalVersionUnsupported.
SIGKILL during op 3 leaves the journal; next start rolls back to the pre-apply state, or completes when all ops were recorded done, before any screen is interactive.
A ChangeSet that fails validation (PathCollision, empty ops, stale expected hash) writes no journal and no operation row.
notes: Decisions 5/6: journals in `.state/`, backups in the caller's operation folder per TC-014. Migration TC-009 builds on this.

title: DB rebuild and corrupt-database recovery tests
description: Add an integration suite over TF-019 and TF-020: (a) delete agentuna.db, rebuild, and compare normalized derived rows with a cold-scan baseline; (b) truncate or flip bytes in the db file and assert quarantine to agentuna.db.corrupt-<ts>, fresh db creation and derived rebuild; (c) preserve operations, operation_files, backups, health_checks, drift_events, preset_applications, preset_application_members and settings across rebuild and quarantine; (d) simulate a crash during rebuild and assert the previous derived state survives; (e) assert WAL replay after a killed process keeps committed rows. Run with a 3k-item fixture and a temp AppPaths, never the real home.
acceptance: Rebuild from a deleted db yields a normalized dump identical to the cold-scan baseline and history table counts unchanged.
A corrupted db file is quarantined with a timestamped name, a new db starts, and the recovery warning names the quarantine path.
A killed rebuild process leaves the previous derived data queryable and the next rebuild succeeds idempotently.
History tables listed in the description survive rebuild and corruption recovery with identical row counts and contents.
The suite runs in under 60 seconds and leaves no quarantine, temp or -wal files in the temp home.
notes: Tests only; implementation is TF-019/TF-020. Uses TF-010 fixtures.
